clue.text: Song she sang about bishop where 2 etc found?

definitions.note: 2 Down is MINT, a herb; this is the place where herbs are found

indicators.note: goes round the outside, so the bishop is placed within

parts.note: a song she sang is her aria
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An opera singer performs an aria around a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the singer's song round the bishop. The definition leans on 2 Down, a herb, and asks where such plants are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbarium is a collection of dried plant specimens, so mint and other herbs would be kept there.

clue.text: Perfect coin

explanation.surface: A flawless coin, as a collector would prize it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in mint condition is pristine; the Mint strikes coins, and to mint means to coin.

clue.text: Audible tunes for king or queen, say

indicators.note: heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: lieder are German art songs

explanation.surface: Songs one can hear performed for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: LIEDER (German songs) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is the head of state, an example of someone at the head of a nation.

clue.text: Understand cricketing term — clear

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone trying to grasp a piece of cricket jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: To get over a hurdle is to clear it, to pass over the obstacle.

clue.text: King Lear, his head in conclusion off?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
gone off, spoilt, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Wondering whether King Lear lost his head at the end of the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the scramble of the two words that follow C. The question mark nods to Charles I losing his head on the scaffold.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles I was King of England, Scotland and Ireland, executed by beheading in 1649.

clue.text: Wrongly accused, as one hopes those leaving theatre have been

definitions.meaning: framed for something one did not do

definitions.text: as one hopes those leaving theatre have been
definitions.meaning: patients leaving an operating theatre should have had their wounds sewn closed

explanation.surface: Someone falsely accused, contrasted with patients leaving surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' is the operating theatre, not a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Being framed is informally being stitched up; surgical wounds are stitched up after an operation.

clue.text: Conspire with saintly bishop, a debt to resolve

parts.note: St Aidan was the bishop who founded Lindisfarne

indicators.note: the letters are to be worked out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A holy bishop schemes to settle what he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to resolve' rearranges A DEBT into DABET.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid and abet is to help someone commit a crime, being complicit in it.

clue.text: Knight feeding waterbird to queen, say?

indicators.note: given into, so the bird goes inside the other word

parts.note: a queen is an example of a bee
a diver is a diving water bird, the loon

explanation.surface: A chess knight is fed a waterbird and passed to the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen, say' is a queen bee, not a monarch or chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Bedivere is one of King Arthur's Knights of the Round Table, who returned Excalibur to the lake.

clue.text: A thin peg, originally designed, that's pushed into hair

indicators.note: arranged to a new plan, so the letters are reordered
at its origin, the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A slim peg of novel design made for sticking into hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes P from peg; 'designed' rearranges A THIN P.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatpin is a long pin pushed through a hat and the hair to keep the hat in place.

clue.text: See 7
Aged aristo sacked, thank God

indicators.note: plundered, thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Relief that an elderly aristocrat has been dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deo gratias is Latin for thanks be to God, used in the liturgy.

clue.text: Queen behind an old faithful companion, briefly backing high street trader

indicators.note: coming after, so the queen's letters follow the rest
going backwards, so the word is reversed
cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a corgi, the breed long kept by the late Queen
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The Queen trails her old corgi while supporting a local shopkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter, 'backing' reverses, and 'behind' puts ER after. The late Queen famously kept corgis.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper selling food, a typical high street business.

clue.text: Content of computer wiper twice by me, ie foolishly in online fraud?

indicators.note: done in a silly way, so the letters are jumbled
the remaining pair of letters is used two times
something that wipes out, removing the content

parts.note: the inside of the word computer, all but its ends

explanation.surface: A computer-wiping program as part of an internet scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content of computer wiper' removes OMPUTE to leave CR; 'twice' gives CRCR; 'foolishly' jumbles that with BY ME IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cybercrime is illegal activity carried out using computers or the internet, such as scams.

clue.text: Protection from sunlight certainly possessed in centre of Greece

indicators.note: placed inside the following letters
the central letters of the word

parts.note: yes, an emphatic affirmative
had, owned

explanation.surface: Something owned in central Greece to keep off the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes the middle two letters of the six-letter country; 'in' sets the other pieces between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeshade is a visor worn to shield the eyes from bright light.

clue.text: Castles for female player

parts.note: two famous Castles, one a Labour cabinet minister and one a royal residence in Berkshire, together name an actress

explanation.surface: Chess castles moved for a woman at the board.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Castle was a Labour cabinet minister; Windsor Castle is a royal home. Together they name an English actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Windsor was a British actress, known for Carry On films and EastEnders.

clue.text: Register right, make changes again

parts.note: a gauge reads a value, registering it
just, fair

explanation.surface: Record the correct figure and amend it once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To readjust is to alter or adapt something a second time.

clue.text: See 15
Number of balls thrown, grey

parts.note: an over in cricket is six balls bowled
cast, flung

explanation.surface: A set of balls hurled in cricket under dull skies.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is dull and cloudy, grey in colour.

clue.text: Japanese food English lady eats in the morning

indicators.note: takes inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady
AM, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman's breakfast of something Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: Edamame are young soybeans in the pod, a Japanese snack.

clue.text: King or queen, say, cutting fruit, one might eat it all

indicators.note: slicing into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a gourd is a fruit of the squash family
chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: A monarch slicing fruit, perhaps to eat the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King or queen' are chess pieces, i.e. men, not royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is a greedy eater, someone who would finish everything.

clue.text: Playwright I harm

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
ill, damage

explanation.surface: A dramatist confessing to doing damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was an American dramatist, author of Long Day's Journey into Night.

clue.text: Place keeping masks etc in pawn

indicators.note: holding within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to put is to place
PPE, personal protective equipment

explanation.surface: Somewhere masks and similar items are left in hock.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is someone used by others, a tool manipulated like a marionette.

clue.text: Kind of delivery from the east of Germany into China

indicators.note: put inside the following word

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, a pal
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: A shipment from eastern Germany to China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Postal delivery is the delivery of letters and parcels by the mail service.

clue.text: Kings for author

parts.note: two names borne by several English kings make the name of a novelist

explanation.walkthrough: Henry and James are both royal names held by several English kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was an American-born novelist, author of The Portrait of a Lady.

clue.text: White pawn

explanation.surface: A chess move: the white player's pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is Rhine white wine; to hock goods is to pawn them for a loan.

clue.text: Clue in Telegraph intractable

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: A tough crossword clue in a rival newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters spanning TelegrapH INTractable.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint is a clue, a small pointer towards an answer.

clue.text: Lovely island castle

parts.note: glam, glamorous

explanation.surface: A beautiful castle on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamis Castle is in Angus, Scotland, linked to Macbeth and the Queen Mother.

clue.text: Parsimony has got queen into trouble

indicators.note: goes inside the following word

parts.note: a mess, a fix
Queen Anne, British monarch 1702-1714

explanation.surface: Stinginess has landed a queen in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony is extreme reluctance to spend, the same as stinginess.
